facts.text: Topaz Ranch Estates began in the late 1960s when John and Virgie Arden bought land at Antelope Valley’s northern edge, creating Fairfield Ranch—now the Sleeping Elephant area.
The community sits in southern Douglas County along Nevada State Route 208, 8 miles east of Wellington and 3 miles west of U.S. Route 395 at Holbrook Junction.
July highs average 87°F, while January lows hover around 23°F, with temperatures rarely dropping below 11°F.
The area receives about 7.3 inches of annual precipitation, mostly winter snowfall, supporting a sparse sagebrush steppe that covers over 95% of the landscape within two miles.
Topaz Ranch Estates faces a very high wildfire risk—over 98% of U.S. communities—highlighted by the 2012 fire that scorched more than 7,000 acres.
The first permanent home appeared in 1968 when Walter and Ann Long built a house on what is now Walker View, marking the community’s initial settlement.
